analysis.title: Asia Tech Strategy: Roadmap to recovery
key_insights: Asian Tech stocks are back to Jul-26 levels, the fourth 20%+ correction in this rally since 2022. JPM stays optimistic on the AI Infra Tech trade for the next 3-6 months, based on 200+ investor meetings.

JPM's three reasons for optimism: unit economics, AI scaling laws and token demand growth remain strong. Valuations have corrected to levels that signal imminent EPS cuts, which JPM thinks are unlikely. Classic cycle-peak signals (inventory builds, shortening lead times, rapid capacity ramp-up) are largely absent.

Investor concerns center on AI infra capex funding, especially at neoclouds, given rising compute commitments from AI labs and hyperscalers and growing reliance on external funding. A smaller group worries about datacenter power availability, especially in the US, and a GPU chip inventory buildup.
Bullish investors want signposts on the next application that can drive AI lab revenue growth beyond coding.

Asian Tech valuations have corrected to mean levels despite accelerating EPS revisions, so stocks already price in a turn in EPS momentum. 3Q26 earnings produced further upward revisions. Investors widely fear 2028 hyperscaler AI capex cuts that would make 2027 the peak. JPM expects hyperscaler capex to stay robust with ample funding avenues.

Unit economics are the best of this cycle across hardware, public clouds and AI model vendors. Model vendors earn significant inference gross margins, clouds benefit from rising $ per Watt compute prices, and hardware benefits from price increases. Compute pricing has not corrected in the past three weeks of neocloud funding worry.

AI scaling laws are intact and possibly accelerating, with multiple new frontier models in the past 3-4 months. Labs expect recursive self-improvement to speed up model gains. Labs are putting a rising share of token budgets into training. JPM reads this as a signal of new TAMs.

Token demand is growing about 17x YoY and re-accelerated after the Aug-Sep wobble. Token prices have resumed falling after a 2Q26 rise, but the long-term norm is a 70-80% annual price decline, which JPM says does not signal weak compute demand.

Compute supply remains extremely constrained and JPM expects it to worsen into 2027. Short-term compute contracts have risen steadily over three months. JPM reads neocloud stress as a market share shift in GPU rental, with larger players such as SpaceX and other hyperscalers gaining share, not a drop in overall GPU demand.

Aggregate hyperscaler public cloud growth accelerated to about 50% YoY after 3Q26 earnings, adding $130bn in revenue. JPM's IT hardware team expects about 70% growth in hyperscaler datacenter capex in 2027, after 85% in 2026.

The semi cycle is the longest ever at 36 months of YoY revenue growth, but JPM sees no GPU/ASIC inventory buildup, component lead times are still lengthening, and capacity growth into 2027 is rational. Supply should ramp in 2028-29.

Next catalysts: Asian tech EPS revisions should stay positive for six months, with about 80% of companies seeing upward revisions. Since the market already prices some cuts, further upgrades should lift stocks. New AI lab applications (enterprise workflow, biomedical, personal agents such as Muse or Dot, multimodal) are a second catalyst.

Risks: a snowball effect if neocloud funding stress releases large amounts of uncommitted GPU compute, compute price ($/W) compression, and datacenter buildout impediments that would show up as replacement of older GPUs (A100, H100) with newer chips. JPM currently sees only mid-to-long-term lease renewals for older hardware.

JPM prefers sub-sectors with positive second derivatives and emerging price-hike narratives into 2027: IC substrate, OSATs, select foundries such as VIS, logic-focused SPE and AI-exposed MLCCs. A price-increase narrative is forming in Taiwan ODMs. It also likes MediaTek for its ASIC pipeline.
Memory valuations are near 1.0x price-to-book and could bounce near term, but investor feedback is mixed on HBM content de-spec concerns. Memory margins are close to peaking.

TW Tech has been more resilient than KR and JP Tech in the correction because of broader EPS exposure and a higher TSMC weight. It could crack if fundamental demand worsens, since negative data points tend to show up first in the Taiwan supply chain.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 earnings season brought further upward EPS revisions for Asian tech, with about 80% of companies seeing upward revisions vs 3 months prior.
Aggregate hyperscaler public cloud growth accelerated to about 50% YoY after 3Q26 earnings, adding $130bn in public cloud revenue (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle per Figure 1 notes).
JPM expects Asian tech EPS revisions to stay broadly positive over the next six months on better pricing and improving margins. Memory margins are close to peaking, unlike the rest of the sector.
risk_factors: Neocloud funding gap could produce uncommitted GPU compute and a snowball effect on GPU demand.
Compute price ($/W) compression would signal weaker demand from AI labs and applications.
Datacenter power constraints, especially in the US, could shift the bottleneck away from chips. This would show up as replacement of older GPUs with newer ones.
Hyperscaler capex could be cut in 2028 on funding and monetization concerns.
Supply ramping in 2028-29 could change the demand-supply gap.
HBM content de-spec concerns weigh on memory sentiment.
TW tech resilience could crack if fundamental demand worsens.
vol_and_positioning: Asian Tech valuations have corrected to mean levels, and JPM says the market is pricing in an EPS cut within six months and a likelihood of hyperscaler capex cuts in 2028.
Investors widely fear 2027 is the peak of hyperscaler capex.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong ROIs mean incremental datacenter projects with contractual commitments still get funded. Compute pricing has not corrected, and freed compute is quickly absorbed by larger players such as SpaceX.
tension_points.bear_case: Neocloud funding stress and heavy reliance on external funding could free uncommitted GPU compute in a repetitive way. That could snowball into weaker GPU demand and a fundamental downturn. Investors also fear 2028 hyperscaler capex cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large pockets of uncommitted GPU compute emerging in 2027, or compute prices ($/W) falling.

tension_points.bull_case: GPU and accelerator compute remains the bottleneck into 2027 and early-mid 2028, and lack of chip inventory in the chain helps manage risk.
tension_points.bear_case: US power constraints could shift the bottleneck away from chips and leave GPU inventory unused.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscalers and neoclouds replacing older GPUs (A100, H100) with newer chips (GB300, VR200) instead of renewing leases on old hardware.
